title: Acting President Iliana Yotova Wins Bulgaria's Presidential Runoff
dek: Initial counts give Yotova about 58% against about 38% for former interim prime minister Andrey Gyurov, who conceded. Official results are not expected until Monday.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Parliament Square in Sofia, Bulgaria (file photo)

keyPoints: Acting President Iliana Yotova is the apparent winner of Bulgaria's presidential runoff, according to initial results counted on Sunday, AP reported.
Counts by several polling agencies gave Yotova about 58% and Andrey Gyurov about 38%. Gyurov conceded, AP reported.
If confirmed, Yotova, 62, would be Bulgaria's first elected female head of state. She took over the presidency in January when Rumen Radev stepped down to run for parliament.
Radev's Progressive Bulgaria party endorsed Yotova. It holds 131 of 240 seats in parliament, an outright majority, Euronews and AP reported.
body:
Acting President Iliana Yotova is the apparent winner of Bulgaria's presidential runoff, according to initial results of the vote count on Sunday, the Associated Press reported. Former interim Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov conceded defeat.

## The result

According to the count by several polling agencies, Yotova received about 58% of the vote and Gyurov, backed by the reformist, pro-Western opposition, was trailing at around 38%, AP reported. Euronews and Deutsche Welle also reported Yotova as the projected winner. Official results were not expected before Monday.

Gyurov said "this is how the Bulgarian citizens have voted" and that the results had to be accepted as they stood, AP reported.

## Who she is and what it means

Yotova, 62, took over the presidency in January, when Radev stepped down to run for parliament, and was seeking her own elected mandate. If the result is confirmed, she would be the first woman elected to Bulgaria's presidency, AP reported.

The vote was the first major test for Prime Minister Radev's Moscow-friendly Progressive Bulgaria party, which endorsed her. The party won 131 of 240 seats in April's parliamentary election, AP reported. AP and observers quoted by it said a Yotova win would keep the presidency in the hands of the governing majority, which some warn could weaken checks and balances.

Bulgaria's presidency is mostly ceremonial. The president leads the armed forces and can veto legislation, but major policy must be approved by parliament, AP reported.

## Foreign policy

AP reported that Yotova is expected to keep Bulgaria on its European path while supporting better relations with Russia and the lifting of sanctions. Bulgaria joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007. Speaking after she voted, Yotova said she wanted a Bulgaria that makes its own decisions and a "strong state with its own foreign policy in a strong Europe," AP reported.

During a television debate, Yotova argued that "peace could come only through negotiations" in Ukraine and proposed a security meeting of all six Black Sea countries to agree a moratorium on hostilities, AP reported. Euronews reported that the war in Ukraine played a significant role in the campaign.

The count is preliminary. Meridian will update this story when official results are published.
